text.p: Tower Semiconductor Ltd has rejected a bid from a U.S. shareholder to acquire the company for $10 a share, the Globes financial newspaper reported.
The offer from U.S. investment advisers Chapman Capital, which holds less than five percent of Tower, values the company at $130 million but is 27 percent below the company's equity capital.
The shares on Nasdaq were last quoted at $6-3/4.
The Israeli newspaper said the company had $108.3 million in cash and short-term deposits at the end of the second quarter.
Tower officials in Israel would not comment on the report.
But Globes quoted the company's co-chief executive Yoav Nissan-Cohen as saying there was such an offer but that management believed the true share value was much higher than the price quoted.
The offer from Chapman came in the form of a letter to Tower chairman George Morgenstern and not an actual attempt to buy the company, the newspaper noted.
The Israel Corp and Data Systems & Software Inc together hold about 40 percent of the Israeli maker of semiconductor integrated circuits.
